evidence_quotes.quote: O estudo sobre os investimentos foi realizado por meio de banco de dados dessas instituições financeiras fornecido pela Secretaria Nacional de Saneamento Ambiental do Ministério das Cidades. Avaliou-se o período de 2004 a 2008.
Os critérios de alocação de recursos do FGTS para cada unidade da federação são definidos pelo seu Conselho Curador.

Embora os investimentos do Governo Federal venham se ampliando, os dados sugerem que ainda persiste uma desigualdade do acesso aos recursos não onerosos e onerosos entre as macrorregiões brasileiras. Os pequenos municípios e a região Norte, onde os déficits são maiores, continuam com dificuldades de acesso aos recursos.

Borja (2011) avaliou que diversos fatores contribuem para essa realidade, a saber: falta de capacidade dos pequenos municípios de elaborar projetos e solicitar financiamento; não enquadramento dos municípios nas regras de acesso aos recursos; dificuldades de atender as diretrizes do Conselho Curador do FGTS, que não dialogam com as necessidades do saneamento básico, tanto em termos do público-alvo, como na distribuição dos recursos entre os componentes.

criterion_notes.c1: Background sections cite secondary national/regional IBGE (2010, 2012) and Moraes et al. (2011) statistics on water and sanitation deficits, but the study itself empirically examines municipal and regional access to federal sanitation investment funds ('acesso aos recursos'), not household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2, the paper discusses legal, administrative, and institutional governance factors in Brazilian sanitation policy (creation of the Ministry of Cities, Law 11.445/2007, parliamentary budget amendments, and FGTS/Caixa and CMN credit-allocation and municipal borrowing eligibility rules). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading, Criterion 2 is NOT satisfied ('no'): the 'regras de acesso e critérios de elegibilidade' analyzed are intergovernmental capital-lending and fiscal/indebtedness rules governing which municipalities and utilities obtain federal investment financing, alongside macro-political commentary on fiscal adjustment and privatization, rather than rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community service access. Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall decision remains 'exclude' because no water or sanitation service-access outcome is empirically measured (c4 = no).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains descriptive empirical analysis of administrative public-finance databases covering Brazilian federal non-onerous budget execution (Sigplan-MPOG and Siga Brasil, 2003-2010) and onerous sanitation credit contracts (FGTS-Caixa and FAT-BNDES, 2004-2009), paired with political-economy discussion.
criterion_notes.c4: Reported empirical outcomes are federal budgetary transfers as a share of GDP, committed/contracted/disbursed non-onerous and onerous investment volumes (R$ billions) across macro-regions and sanitation subsectors, parliamentary amendment shares, and the population/HDI/GDP profile of 570 municipalities awarded Caixa (FGTS) contracts. It does not report empirical outcomes for water or sanitation service access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or household exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Within its public-finance scope, the units of analysis (federal budget actions/programs and 570 municipalities contemplated with FGTS-Caixa contracts), stratifying/institutional factors (funding modality, macro-region, municipal population/HDI/GDP), investment outcomes, and descriptive administrative-data design are clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Descriptive quantitative analysis of federal budgetary and development-bank administrative databases combined with political-economy policy analysis
population_and_sample: Federal sanitation budget programs/actions (2003-2010) and Brazilian municipalities awarded FGTS-Caixa sanitation financing contracts (N = 570 municipalities with identified names, 2004-2009)
exposure: Federal sanitation financing policy, macro-fiscal budget allocation (non-onerous OGU vs. onerous FGTS-Caixa and FAT-BNDES credit), parliamentary amendments, and municipal/provider credit-eligibility and borrowing rules (2003-2010)
outcome: Federal budgetary commitments and disbursements (% of GDP and R$ billions) by region and sanitation component, and distribution of FGTS-Caixa financing contracts across Brazilian municipalities by population size, HDI, and GDP per capita
rationale: Although the abstract mentions 'access rules and eligibility criteria' ('regras de acesso e critérios de elegibilidade'), full-text inspection shows that both the rules and the empirical outcomes concern municipal and utility access to federal capital-investment funds (OGU grants and FGTS-Caixa / FAT-BNDES loans), not household or community access to water or sanitation services. Empirically, the study tracks federal budget shares, R$ contracted/disbursed across macro-regions and sanitation subsectors, and the socio-economic profile of 570 municipalities receiving Caixa/FGTS contracts, comparing investment targeting only descriptively against background regional deficit statistics. It therefore lacks a water or sanitation service-access outcome (E04; c1 = no, c4 = no) and also fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 (c2 = no), while remaining an exclusion under the plain wording of Criterion 2 as well.
